q: What emission factor per tonne-km should I use for road freight in India?
title: Truck freight factor per tonne-km, India
short: Use the default factor for India for your truck class, per tonne-km and well-to-wheel: from 0.3795 kg CO2e for a small pickup down to 0.0551 for a tractor-trailer. These defaults already include typical empty running, so do not add the return trip. A carrier's own factor, backed by fuel data, is better still.

sections.h: Default factors for India by truck class
ul: Small truck or pickup, under 3.5 t GVW, diesel: 0.3795 kg CO2e per tonne-km.
Light truck, 3 to 5 t GVW, diesel: 0.2222.
Medium truck, 5 to 12 t GVW, diesel: 0.1400.
Heavy truck, 12 to 20 t GVW, diesel: 0.0902.
Heavy truck, 20 to 30 t GVW, diesel: 0.0823.
Heavy truck, 30 to 50 t GVW, diesel: 0.0663.
p: Each value is well-to-wheel, at average load including typical empty running. Other fuels differ: a medium truck on CNG is 0.1689, and a small pickup is 0.4124 on petrol and 0.4920 on CNG.
Pick the class of the vehicle that actually carried the goods. The India defaults are subject to revision, so recheck them each reporting year.

sections.h: Which data to use, in order of preference
ol: Fuel records for the vehicles that carried your goods, allocated by tonne-km. This is the most accurate.
Your carrier's own factor per tonne-km for that lane, if they can show the fuel and tonne-km behind it. Use it as given.
The default factor for India for the truck class, from the list above.

ul: Per vehicle-km or per vehicle-mile: the factor has no load in it. Divide it by the average tonnes actually carried, empty trips included, to get per tonne-km. Convert per vehicle-mile to per vehicle-km first by dividing by 1.609. Never multiply a per vehicle factor by your tonnes and distance.
Per short ton-mile, common in US tables: divide by 1.46 to get per tonne-km, because one short ton-mile is 1.46 tonne-km.

sections.h: Do not add the return trip again
p: The defaults are averages over real operations, empty kilometres included. Adding an empty return uplift, or scaling by a load factor, on top of them counts the empty running twice. You count empty kilometres yourself only when you build a factor from your own fuel data, as below.

sections.h: Building a factor from your own trips
p: kg CO2 per tonne-km = (litres per km x 2.68) x (total km driven / loaded km) / average payload in tonnes.
Truck size, load and empty return change the answer more than anything else. A half-empty truck has roughly twice the per tonne-km factor of a full one.

Diesel burnt at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre gives tank-to-wheel CO2. The defaults are well-to-wheel CO2e, which adds emissions from producing and delivering the fuel, so they are higher. Do not mix the two in one total, and label which one you use.

ul: Part loads: allocate the trip's emissions by your share of tonne-km, not by your share of the freight bill.
Volume-limited cargo: if the truck is full by volume, use your share of space, and say so.
No weight on the bill: take weight from the invoice or packing list, not from the freight amount.

example.title: Worked example: a 1,000 km trip with a 16 tonne load
lines: Assumed fuel economy: 3.5 km per litre, loaded and empty
Empty running: 25 percent extra, so 1,250 km driven for 1,000 loaded km
Own trip factor: 957.1 / 16,000 = 0.060 kg CO2 per tonne-km, tank-to-wheel
Default for comparison: a 16 t load fits the heavy truck 20 to 30 t GVW class, 0.0823 kg CO2e per tonne-km, well-to-wheel
16,000 x 0.0823 = 1,316.8 kg CO2e, with empty running already included
example.note: Fuel economy and empty running are assumptions; replace them with your carrier's figures. The two results differ because the default is well-to-wheel and reflects average Indian loading, while the trip figure is tank-to-wheel for one assumed trip. Use one basis, not both.

senseible: Senseible's logistics calculator works per tonne-km by mode and by Indian truck class, using the default factors for India. A carrier's own factor is used as given, and no extra empty return uplift is added to any default. Freight invoices read in Senseible are kept as Scope 3 evidence.
